analytic: After a proper post-exceptional L cut, every ordinary L consumes a different bridge of the COMPLETE entry active component. All temporary R imports are discarded on the departure side by exact inheritance. Thus at most c ordinary blocks, each at most3 updates, precede the next exceptional block of at most5 updates: gap<=3c+5. If no exceptional block existed, this finite old-edge supply and the at-most-four-R rule would be contradicted.

Epochs are actual cut intervals[s_i,s_(i+1)), with s_i=tau_i+1. For birth update b and death update d, nu(d+1)-nu(b) counts exceptional L updates in[b,d]. Birth is R, so no birth-boundary ambiguity. The death can itself be exceptional, only making the upper count j+1 conservative. The intersected epoch lengths cover the full lifetime, yielding the displayed weighted bound.

Beginning after the first exceptional L removes the only initial partial-epoch convention. Under eventual renewal-entry mass cap M and consumed renewal lag cap J, age<=(J+1)(3M+5), despite arbitrarily large dormant archives or intermediate active R imports.

After finitely many checkpoint-current lifetimes have their final future consumption, every later L obeys this age bound. The retained exact suffix predictor therefore yields eventual nonzero translation, not104. Conversely non-eventual translation requires unbounded renewal-entry masses in every tail or, when those masses are eventually bounded, unbounded renewal lags among late-born consumed lifetimes.
